articles.title: Carabao Cup quarter-final draw: Liverpool host Bournemouth as Bradford and Fleetwood get home ties against Premier League opposition
articles.summary: Carabao Cup quarter-final draw as Liverpool to face Bournemouth; League One Bradford City and League Two Fleetwood Town both get homes ties against Premier League opposition; games will be played on week of December 14
articles.body:
Fleetwood Town's reward for knocking out Premier League champions Arsenal is a home game against the winner of Everton vs Newcastle on Thursday night.

Crystal Palace will host Sunderland in an all-Premier League clash in the remaining last-eight tie.

Liverpool beat Chelsea on penalties to set up a meeting with Andoni Iraola's former side Bournemouth, who went through to the quarter-finals in style with a fine 3-0 win against Aston Villa.

Manchester City also needed penalties to earn victory against Brighton. Their opponents, Bradford, beat Peterborough 2-0.

Eddie Nketiah got the only goal of the game as Palace won at Fulham.

Sunderland also beat Premier League opposition to take their place in the next round as they overcame Brentford 3-2.

The quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup will take place during the week commencing December 14.

articles.title: Vincent Kompany Released from Hospital After Collapsing at Bayern Munich Training
articles.summary: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany was released from the hospital Wednesday after he was initially admitted for collapsing during a training session on Friday.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany was released from the hospital Wednesday after he was initially admitted for collapsing during a training session on Friday.

His release comes after the club said in an official statement on Friday that Kompany collapsed during the second string session, received medical attention and will "undergoing thorough examinations" in the hospital for the time being.

Max Eberl, director of sport for Bayern Munich, told German broadcaster ARD on Wednesday (h/t ESPN ), "Given the circumstances, he's doing ⁠well. He ‌was discharged from the hospital [Wednesday]. That is the biggest and best news for all of ‌us.

"It's a meningeal irritation that caused this incident on Friday. He will now rest and take medication, and I am certain that he will ⁠very soon be back on the touchline, operating at 100%."

Eberl previously issued a statement in the club's Friday release:

"Vincent Kompany's health is our top priority. We at FC Bayern will do everything we can to ensure he makes a speedy recovery. Vinnie is receiving all the necessary medical care and support, and all the time he needs. His coaching team, in whom we have complete confidence, will take over his duties. All of us at FC Bayern wish Vinnie a speedy recovery."

Other members of the coaching staff will handle Kompany's duties while he is out.

Kompany has been Bayern Munich's head coach since May 2024. He has a 91-19-12 record with the club. Bayern's next match is Saturday against Borussia Dortmund.

articles.title: Eder Sarabia, nuevo entrenador del Espanyol
articles.standfirst: El conjunto perico anuncia el sustituto de Manolo González. Firma hasta 2028
articles.summary: El conjunto perico anuncia el sustituto de Manolo González. Firma hasta 2028
articles.body: El RCD Espanyol ha anunciado la llegada de Eder Sarabia como nuevo entrenador tras la destitución de Manolo González anoche tras caer en Copa del Rey ante el modesto Sestao River en la prórroga. El exentrenador del Elche y el Andorra ha llegado a un acuerdo con el conjunto blanquiazul para convertirse en el entrenador del primer equipo hasta el 30 de junio de 2028. Junto a Eder Sarabia, también se incorporan al cuerpo técnico Jon López, Jon Moreno, Aitor Unzué y Álvaro González. De este modo, el exfutbolista cántabro, que defendió la camiseta blanquiazul en 82 ocasiones, vuelve a la disciplina perica . La presentación oficial como nuevo entrenador del Espanyol tendrá lugar el próximo martes, por lo que se confirma que Sergio García, del filial, dirigirá al equipo de manera interina esta jornada ante el Villarreal.

articles.title: Jon Uriarte: "El Athletic se ha situado como el cuarto club con mejor rendimiento de España"
articles.standfirst: El presidente se dirige a los compromisarios que toman parte en la Asamblea General
articles.summary: El presidente se dirige a los compromisarios que toman parte en la Asamblea General
articles.body: El Athletic celebra en la sala principal del Palacio Euskalduna la Asamblea General Ordinaria de Socios Compromisarios, que ha comenzado con 426 de ellos presentes en la sala o inscritos en la reunión de manera telemática, La Asamblea ha comenzado con un minuto de silencio en recuerdo de las víctimas del grave accidente de tren de Toledo. El presidente Jon Uriarte ha tomado la palabra antes de dar inicio al seguimiento de los distintos puntos del orden del día con un discurso en el que ha resaltado que “hemos puesto toda nuestra dedicación para que Lezama sea un centro de desarrollo de cantera a nivel mundial. En estas últimas cuatro temporadas el Athletic se ha situado como el cuarto club con mejor rendimiento de España”. En un momento de su intervención Uriarte ha celebrado la designación de Simón como mejor portero del mundo y la sala ha dedicado aplausos al guardameta rojblanco. El dirigente rojiblanco se mostró especialmente orgulloso del momento de formación. “La prueba evidente de salud en nuestro centro de formación está en el número de canteranos que son internacionales En el fútbol masculino ha pasado de 6 a 16 y en el femenino de 5 a 18. No son datos que se den consecuencia de la casualidad, sino de profesionales y la inversión en Lezama, que supera los 15 millones por temporada”. El presidente Uriarte no echó sólo flores a su gestión. “La pasada temporada no cumplimos los objetivos marcados con resultados por debajo de nuestras expectativas. La consecuencia inmediata has sido un descenso en el valor de mercado de nuestra plantilla, que ha caído un 37% situándose en el que había entre las temporadas 22-23 y 23-34”, resaltó. Y también señaló que para repuntar en todos esos aspectos es “fundamental un mejor rendimiento tanto del talento retenido como en los fichajes realizados, con inversiones muy importantes que en algunos casos no hemos conseguido que aporten una mejora regular y diferencial”.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin wants to know why LSU-Alabama kickoff isn't scheduled for prime time
articles.summary: Kiffin does not buy the conspiracy theory that the SEC wants LSU to win.
articles.body:
LSU and Alabama will play next weekend as Lane Kiffin takes on the Crimson Tide for the first time as the Tigers' head coach.

Both teams have a bye this weekend, but the game will kick off next week at 3:30 p.m. ET, or 2:30 p.m. locally in Baton Rouge.

Kiffin was asked Wednesday about what he thought about the rivalry game getting the mid-afternoon slot.

"I was like, well, if someone thinks the SEC wants us to win this year after what's been going on, they must have just been on Mars the last four months," Kiffin said in his Wednesday press conference. "So I guess when I look at it that way, I'm not surprised. "Especially in 16 years, this game has been at night here all the time. I never even considered that it wouldn't be at night. So I guess that's probably naive of me."

"I was like, well, if someone thinks the SEC wants us to win this year after what's been going on, they must have just been on Mars the last four months," Kiffin said in his Wednesday press conference. "So I guess when I look at it that way, I'm not surprised.

"Especially in 16 years, this game has been at night here all the time. I never even considered that it wouldn't be at night. So I guess that's probably naive of me."

The last time these teams played a non-night game was in 2019, with a 2:42 p.m. CT kickoff, but it was held in Tuscaloosa. Kiffin is correct that the last time this rivalry game had a non-night kickoff in Baton Rouge was in 2010, when it kicked off at 2:30 p.m. CT locally.

While LSU vs. Alabama will be one of the biggest games of the week on Nov. 7, the time slot may have been chosen so it doesn't compete directly with another marquee matchup, Miami at Notre Dame, set for a 7:30 p.m. start time on NBC. LSU vs. Alabama will be aired on ABC.

LSU and the SEC butting heads dominated the offseason. The Tigers attempted to add Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris to the roster, even though both players had left their college programs and participated in NFL training camps.

The contention between the two sides grew to the point that, if Wright and Harris played for the Tigers, the SEC would vote to expel LSU from the conference.

Wright and Harris were never added to the Tigers roster, but the school and conference remain at odds, this time over men's basketball. LSU argues that RJ Luis Jr. should be eligible to play for the program after going undrafted. Luis did sign a two-way contract, but did not appear in any G League games, and an injunction was granted allowing him to return to the Tigers.

These fights between the school and the conference are what Kiffin is referring to, and it seems the LSU head coach believes the league is using this afternoon kickoff as a pseudo-punishment.

articles.title: Los Compromisarios dan un aviso a Uriarte y su Junta Directiva
articles.standfirst: Un tercio de la Asamblea cuestiona su gestión durante el último ejercicio
articles.summary: Un tercio de la Asamblea cuestiona su gestión durante el último ejercicio
articles.body: La Junta Directiva del Athletic ha sacado adelante las tres propuestas que ha trasladado a sus socios compromisarios en una Asamblea General Ordinaria que comenzó pasadas las 18 horas y que todavía continúa en el Palacio Euskalduna. Las tres primeras votaciones de la noche han sido para validar la gestión de la Junta Directiva en el último ejercicio, las cuentas en la campaña 25-26 y el presupuesto para la temporada en curso. Uriarte y su grupo de gobierno, reelegidos la pasada primavera sin ningún rival en las urnas, han recibido un tirón de orejas. El resultado a la valoración de la gestión no ha tenido la mayoría búlgara que sí se ha dado en otros aspectos. Así, entre los 627 asistentes en ese momento ha habido 210 votos en contra, lo que supone un tercio de los sufragios. En el foro no ha gustado el tono de una de las respuestas de Uriarte a pregunta de uno de los compromisarios. Ha sido un pequeño toque de atención para una Junta Directiva que ha sacado nota con las cuentas del ejercicio anterior, que tuvo un récord de ingresos en la historia del club con 192,9 millones de euros. Ha habido 421 votos a favor por sólo 98 en contra. La proporción cambió ligeramente en la consideración a un presupuesto para esta temporada de 152,6 millones de euros y una previsión de 3 millones de déficit. La Junta Directiva recibió luz verde con 379 votos a favor y 133 en contra.

articles.title: El Surne Bilbao cede el liderato ante el Alba Berlín
articles.standfirst: Hilliard (21+1+9), Vautier (17+12) y Normantas (15) no evitan la derrota (103-100)
articles.summary: Hilliard (21+1+9), Vautier (17+12) y Normantas (15) no evitan la derrota (103-100)
articles.body: El Surne Bilbao cayó por 103-110 en su visita al Alba Berlín, en la tercera jornada de la Liga de Campeones (BCL), y cedió el liderato del grupo al conjunto alemán en un partido que llegó a dominar por 13 puntos en el tercer cuarto, pero que se le escapó en un desenlace muy igualado. Tras alcanzar el 48-61 nada más comenzar la segunda mitad, el equipo de Jaume Ponsarnau sufrió un profundo bache que permitió al Alba darle la vuelta al marcador y alcanzar una ventaja de nueve puntos (81-72, m.32). Sin embargo, una gran reacción liderada por Darrun Hilliard en el tramo final devolvió la emoción al encuentro y alimentó las esperanzas de victoria del equipo bilbaíno. A falta de 1.12 para el final, el estadounidense igualó el marcador con dos triples consecutivos, pero el Surne no pudo culminar la remontada ante un Alba más sólido en los instantes decisivos. En el conjunto berlinés brilló el ala-pívot Brandon Angel, autor de 24 puntos sin fallo en sus diez lanzamientos de campo, incluidos dos triples. Por parte del Surne, Hilliard fue el más destacado con 21 puntos y nueve rebotes, mientras que Bastien Vautier firmó un doble-doble de 17 puntos y 12 rebotes. El desacierto desde la línea de tiros libres (16 de 25) penalizó también al equipo de Ponsarnau. El encuentro comenzó con un ritmo elevado y un intercambio de canastas muy equilibrado, hasta que el Surne logró ponerse por delante con una canasta de Font que situó el 13-14 en el minuto 6. El equipo bilbaíno afrontó el choque sin Krampelj, descartado para la rotación. El Alba, dirigido por el técnico cordobés Pedro Calles, encontró en el triple su principal argumento para mantenerse en el partido ante un Surne más equilibrado, que encontraba soluciones tanto cerca del aro, con Vautier obligado a multiplicarse por los problemas de faltas de Hlinason, como desde el perímetro, con Normantas y Darling. El conjunto bilbaíno amplió la ventaja desde el 24-26 con el que concluyó el primer cuarto hasta alcanzar rentas de nueve puntos (24-33 y 39-48). El equipo alemán, con Angel y Ford como principales referencias ofensivas, consiguió reducir la diferencia antes del descanso hasta el 43-48. Tras la reanudación, el Surne elevó su ventaja hasta los 13 puntos (48-61), pero el Alba respondió con un demoledor parcial de 33-11 que cambió por completo el escenario del encuentro. Los bilbaínos no se rindieron y, de la mano de Hilliard, llegaron a recuperar la igualdad en los últimos instantes, aunque acabaron cediendo ante la mayor solidez del conjunto berlinés. 103.- Alba Berlín (24+19+31+29): Ford (23), Mattisseck (3), Delow (10), Angel (22), Bean (14) -equipo inicial- Griesel (7), Wieskamp (11), Hermannsson (8), Bennefeld (-), Bohmer (2) y Sima (3). 100.- Surne Bilbao (26+22+24+28): Somogyi (5), Darling (13), Hilliard (21), Ansorregi (7), Vautier (17) -equipo inicial- Normantas (15), Frey (1), Hlinason (8), Hustak (-), Petrasek (11) y Font (2). Árbitros: Ademir Zurapovic (Bosnia), Mihkel Manniste (Estonia) y Josip Jurcevic (Croacia). Eliminaron por cinco faltas a Delow (m.37). Incidencias: partido de la tercera jornada de la Liga de Campeones disputado en el Uber Arena de Berlín. Los jugadores del Surne Bilbao lucieron crespón blanco, en su camiseta negra, en memoria de las víctimas del accidente ferroviario de Toledo.

articles.title: Purdue football will have earliest start ever in 2027 after moving up opener
articles.summary: Purdue football was forced to find a replacement on its 2027 schedule. Now, the Boilers will host their earliest game in program history next season.
articles.body:
WEST LAFAYETTE − Conference schedule expansion in the ACC left North Carolina nixing its trip to play at Purdue's Ross-Ade Stadium in 2027.

Purdue football instead will host Football Championship Subdivision (FCS) program Albany , per a contract agreement signed in January. That information was obtained by the Journal & Courier through a public records request.

Originally scheduled for Sept. 11, 2027, an amended contract signed in August agrees to move the date to Purdue 's season opener on Aug. 28, 2027. It would mark the earliest date for a Purdue game to be played. The Boilermakers have played five times on Aug. 30, most recently against Ball State in 2025.

The date change cost Purdue an additional $75,000, making the total payout to Albany's athletic department $575,000 to host the Great Danes, per the amended contract.

Check out our Purdue football vs Washington photo gallery: Best images

Purdue will now play Miami (Ohio) on Sept. 11, also per an amended contract signed earlier this month. That game was originally scheduled for Sept. 18.

The Boilermakers also are scheduled to travel to Notre Dame on Sept. 4, per a 2017 contract. The six-game contract ends with Notre Dame visiting Purdue on Sept. 23, 2028.

The remaining nine games on the 2027 schedule includes home contests with Illinois, Indiana, Michigan State, Penn State and UCLA along with road games at Maryland, Nebraska, Ohio State and Oregon. The dates for those games will be revealed by the Big Ten Conference at a later time.

articles.title: Chelsea win as Bayern draw with Madrid in Women's Champions League
articles.summary: Goals from Ellie Carpenter and Kadeisha Buchanan were enough to give Chelsea their second win in this season's Women's Champions League on Wednesday to join...
articles.body:
Goals from Ellie Carpenter and Kadeisha Buchanan were enough to give Chelsea their second win in this season's Women's Champions League on Wednesday to join Arsenal and Lyon at the top of the table.

Bayern Munich came from two goals down to draw with Real Madrid while Servette thrashed OH Leuven 5-1.

Chelsea, who reached the final in 2020-21, opened their campaign with a win and a draw despite scoring just once in their first two games.

They looked nailed on for another win in the first half at Plough Lane as they dominated the game without getting a goal.

That changed in the 51st minute when Wieke Kaptein cut the ball back for substitute Carpenter, making her 50th Champions League appearance, who slid the ball under the goalkeeper Rachele Baldi.

Melvine Malard missed a golden chance to put the game to bed but Buchanan made it 2-0 a minute from time, heading Kaptein's cross into the Roma net.

"I'm pleased with the fact we scored really early in the second half. We could probably have killed the game a little bit earlier," said Chelsea coach Sonia Bompastor.

"In these kinds of matches, if you don't kill it off, you just leave the hope for the opponent. When that's the case, they have a lot of energy and confidence.

"It's important for us in these games to be able to be clinical and ruthless as early as possible.

"But we find different ways to impose ourselves in the game and to score goals. So it's good."

Chelsea move to seven points after matchday three, behind Lyon and Arsenal on goal difference. Champions Barcelona, who have six points after winning both of their opening games, will return to the top if they beat HB Koge in Denmark on Thursday.

Marie-Antoinette Katoto scored the first two before Vicki Becho chimed in with a hat-trick off the bench in eight-time winners Lyon's 5-0 home thrashing of Inter Milan.

Arsenal got their campaign up and running with a 3-0 win over Benfica, Alessia Russo netting a hat-trick to become the highest scoring English player in European football with 23 goals.

There was a moment's silence before kick-off at the Sportpark Unterhaching in Munich as a mark of respect after at least 68 people were killed in a train crash near Madrid earlier on Wednesday.

Real Madrid, who were all wearing black armbands, took an early lead when Athenea found the net in the seventh minute.

Former Bayern forward Lineth Beerensteyn doubled the lead 15 minutes later before her old team fought back with an Edna Imade header just after the half-hour.

Momoko Tanikawa equalised in the 52nd minute with a curling shot from the edge of the box and it finished 2-2.

Swiss side Servette dispatched Belgium's Leuven 5-1 with Paola Hernandez and Gloria Marinelli scoring two goals each.

articles.title: SEC carnage: How a deep, versatile conference could force a 3-loss team into the CFP
articles.summary: The Longhorns know each week in the volatile, loaded SEC can bring an end to their CFP hopes. "This is an any-given-Saturday league," Texas DT Hero Kanu said...
articles.body:
Texas football 's four SEC games to date this season have been decided by a combined 16 points. Steve Sarkisian says that's not a coincidence considering the Longhorns' schedule.

Texas' head coach is now in his sixth year with the program, a stretch that includes three seasons in the Big 12 before Texas' 2024 move to the SEC. The new conference brought a whole new world for Texas. Yes, the Longhorns lost multiple conference games with Sarkisian in both the Big 12 in 2021 and 2022 and the SEC in 2025 and 2026. But a closer look reveals a true chasm in conferences.

6:30 p.m. Saturday at Royal-Memorial Stadium.

ESPN; 1300 AM, 98.1 FM, 105.3 FM (Spanish).

The best of the SEC (Georgia) pummeled the best of the Big 12 (TCU) in a 65-7 rout to win the 2022 national championship. The SEC sent three programs to the College Football Playoff in 2024 and five teams to the CFP in 2025, two years in which the conference won a combined eight playoff games. The Big 12 sent just one team to the CFP in each of the last two seasons. Neither registered a victory. Arizona State fought valiantly in a double-overtime loss to Texas in January 2025. Texas Tech then reached the CFP one year later, but lost to Oregon 23-0 last New Year's Day.

The Longhorns' uneven play is one culprit for their middling performance in conference competition. Sarkisian noted a different factor Monday, highlighting an issue that plagues programs across the SEC.

"The transfer portal does two things," Sarkisian said. "One, there's a lot of really good players spread out on a lot of rosters. There's always been good players in our conference; now, more than ever, people have depth and they're versatile. We've got new players too, and we might not have the same depth that maybe the SEC top tier teams had in the past.

"The combination of those two things, I think, adds up to more opportunities for teams to knock teams off if you're not playing your best football that day. Just about everybody's good enough to beat anybody in our league."

Sarkisian said his roster isn't equipped to overpower Texas' fellow SEC foes. The sentiment is echoed by even his most imposing players.

"I think the best (defensive) linemen in the country play in this conference," Texas center Connor Roberston said Monday. "There's no bad teams in this conference. Every week you got to be 100% prepared and focused."

Texas defensive tackle Hero Kanu came to Texas in 2025 after three seasons at Ohio State. The Big Ten, another Power Four conference, is the home of the last three national champions (Indiana, Ohio State and Michigan). The Longhorns' man in the middle still sees the SEC as a different animal.

"This is an any-given-Saturday league," Kanu said. "If you don't go and show out, you're going to lose. You better come prepared every single week."

Texas placed its CFP hopes in precarious position with losses to two unranked SEC teams. The road doesn't get easier in the coming weeks. Texas has five games left, all conference matchups. Three are on the road. A question now looms over the both the Longhorns and the rest of college football: Could a three-loss team qualify for the playoff?

History isn't exactly in Texas' favor. The 12-team CFP has included only one three-loss team in each of the last two seasons, both with extenuating circumstances. Clemson qualified in 2024 after winning the ACC. Alabama qualified in 2025 after recording a third loss in the SEC championship game.

Sarkisian would, of course, prefer the easiest path to the CFP: five successive wins to close the regular season, a scenario in which Texas would likely be playoff-bound regardless of whether it won, lost or sat at home during the SEC championship. But the path to the CFP with three regular-season losses looks more possible by the week. Three two-loss teams (Alabama, Texas and Ole Miss) enter this weekend within the top 12 of the AP poll. The nation's slate of contenders will continue to stack losses by the week, presenting an increasingly complicated picture for the CFP selection committee.

There are just two SEC programs (Kentucky and Georgia) with fewer than two conference losses and they each have three games remaining agaisnt teams ranked in the AP Top 25.

Sarkisian lobbied for Texas to reach the playoff last season, arguing that Texas' challenging schedule made up for its three regular-season losses. A similar pitch could be made this year, though perhaps to greater effect. Texas defeated then-No. 1 Ohio State in September and has logged wins over top-25 teams in Tennessee and Ole Miss, and additional ranked wins could come in upcoming games against LSU and Missouri.

Texas won't be blemish-free when it presents its CFP case. That might not matter in the sport's current era, in which more leeway could be given to teams facing the SEC gantlet.

articles.title: Vincent Kompany: Bayern Munich head coach discharged from hospital after collapsing at training
articles.summary: Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany has been discharged from hospital, says board member for ​sports Max Eberl; the former Man City defender collapsed during a second-team training session on Friday; Kompany had missed some duties earlier in the week due to a viral infection
articles.body:
Kompany was taken to hospital last week after collapsing at Bayern's training ground during ‌a second-team training session.

He missed out on media duties ahead of Bayern's Champions League match against Arsenal due to a viral infection, but did make it to the dugout for the 2-2 draw.

"Given the circumstances, he's doing ⁠well," Eberl told broadcaster ARD ⁠ahead of the German Cup game against Magdeburg, who Bayern beat 6-1. "He ‌was discharged from the hospital today [Wednesday]. That is the biggest and best news for all of ‌us.

"It's a meningeal irritation that caused this incident on Friday. He will now rest and take medication and I am certain that he will ⁠very soon be back on the ​touchline, operating at 100 per cent."

No date has ​been set for Kompany's return, with ​Eberl saying the Belgian would resume his ⁠duties only after receiving medical clearance, something that was reiterated by his assistant, Aaron Danks.

Speaking after the win against Magdeburg, he said: "I still don't feel like there is any timeline on it [when Kompany is back]. It's obviously a really positive step in his road to recovery.

"He gets to settle back at home now, be closer to his family, be closer to his home comforts but it's still really important that he takes his rest and he recovers. So there is no timescale on it. Nothing that I've been told and I've been informed.

"Our doctors will continue to work closely with Vince and at the right moment, he will be back with us once he is fit and healthy to do that and we look forward to that day.

"But in the meantime, we just continue to push forward as a group with the players and staff and keep working hard.

"I haven't spoken to him for a couple of days now so I still think not much has changed in terms of our working relationship at the moment.

"His health is our number one priority and for us he is still in recovery mode so we want him to get back to full health, full fitness and then join us.

"Over the coming days, weeks, I don't know, things will start to move forward and we can start to engage in more of these conversations.

"But there has been no timescale on that at the moment. It is just purely about his health, his recovery and him taking the time that he needs."

articles.title: Big 12 Rule Change Reveals In-Game Penalties for Fan Conduct amid 'Discriminatory Chants' Toward BYU
articles.summary: The Big 12 introduced new rules regarding fan behavior following UCF's 39-31 upset victory over BYU on Saturday.
articles.body:
The Big 12 introduced new rules regarding fan behavior following UCF's 39-31 upset victory over BYU on Saturday.

"The Big 12 Conference has completed its review of the discriminatory chants directed at BYU during Saturday's football game at UCF," the conference said in a statement released Wednesday, via ESPN's Pete Thamel. "While the Conference recognizes the pregame protocols followed by UCF and immediate actions taken during the game, including removal of some individuals responsible for the conduct, discriminatory behavior has no place in the Big 12. The Conference has issued UCF a $100,000 fine, which will be directed toward student education initiatives."

As part of the new rules, a confirmed first incident of discriminatory conduct during a game will result in an automatic minimum $100,000 fine as well as a formal warning.

For a second confirmed incident during the same contest, an in-game competitive penalty such as a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty in football or a technical foul in basketball will be assessed. An additional $500,000 fine may also be included.

Meanwhile, fans ejected from games for discriminatory conduct will be banned from attending all athletic events for the remainder of the academic year.

As UCF picked up a surprising victory over a BYU squad that sat at No. 2 in the AP Top 25 poll prior to the contest, some fans were removed from the game by security for chants directed at the Cougars (h/t David Ubben of The Athletic).

Colorado State similarly issued an apology for chants towards BYU during a 41-23 loss to the Cougars on Sept. 19.

BYU head coach Kalani Sitake addressed the situation after the game.

"Everyone's human and I'm not going to dwell on that. I know amazing people that are Colorado State fans and alumni and I'm just going to focus on the beautiful people that are positives," Sitake said at the time, per USA Today's Kevin Lytle . "You can't judge the entire fan base on a few, so that's what we're going to focus on. The environment here was awesome, the fans were excited about their team."

Now, impermissible fan conduct during Big 12 games could lead to penalties that affect their team's chances of winning.

articles.title: Chelsea Women: How unbeaten Blues are getting back to their best
articles.summary: Chelsea are getting back to their best following their 2-0 Women's Champions League win over Roma - so how have they built success in their unbeaten run?
articles.body:
Chelsea's 2-0 victory over Roma in the Women's Champions League was yet another demonstration they can win in different ways.

Sonia Bompastor's side disappointed last season when they lost their Women's Super League and FA Cup crowns, while rivals Arsenal handed them an exit from Europe at the quarter-final stage.

That followed a dream unbeaten season in which the Blues wrapped up a domestic treble in Bompastor's first year in charge.

Having previously won six successive WSL titles, a blip was inevitable and their transition period highlighted flaws in the new era under their French boss.

There was still optimism in this campaign and, while Bompastor expected it would take more time, Chelsea have started impressively.

They are unbeaten in all competitions, top of the Women's Super League with Manchester City after seven games, and have won two and drawn one of their opening three Champions League phase matches.

"I'm really pleased with the results for sure, but not only the results, I think the different performances," said Bompastor earlier this week.

"Right now, the way we are performing gives us a really good advantage and a big chance to win games."

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

Their 2-0 victory over Roma on Wednesday was well deserved.

A flurry of chances were squandered in a dominant first half before substitute Ellie Carpenter broke the deadlock after 51 minutes.

Chelsea made sure of victory when defender Kadeisha Buchanan nodded in their second just before the end.

"I'm really pleased with the solid performances in terms of the defensive aspects. We have played three games and we haven't conceded," added Bompastor.

"When you want to go far in competitions, it's good to have this solid base. With the quality we have in the team, I'm confident we will always create opportunities."

She admitted the Champions League was "a different level" to what they had already overcome in the WSL and Bompastor has rotated her squad effectively to cope in both competitions.

They seem to have sorted out their defensive leaks that were so evident last season and look more clinical going forward.

Full-back Carpenter has four goals in all competitions, England forward Lauren James is in scintillating form and young midfielder Lexi Potter is developing a flourishing partnership with Lionesses star Keira Walsh.

They look unpredictable, being able to adapt shape in a back three or a back four, and can go direct with the aid of goalkeeper Hannah Hampton's distribution.

They had to grind out their win over Roma in a way that former boss Emma Hayes' sides used to do - proof in itself they have learned from the previous campaign.

"Even when we opened the competition against Austria Vienna, it was a tough game because they were brave and exposed us to some challenges," said Bompastor.

"We found a way to win, but obviously we want to control every game as much as we can, no matter what competition it is.

"Tonight and on Sunday we rotated the team a little bit. We find different ways to impose ourselves in the game and to score goals. That's good."

Chelsea beat Roma to maintain unbeaten start

Manchester City won the WSL title impressively last season but externally, there was an expectation Chelsea would bounce back.

Bompastor was more cautious, insisting they were still transitioning after the departures of big-name players including Sam Kerr, Millie Bright and Guro Reiten.

She said: "You need to consider the fact that Chelsea had the same coach for 12 years. It takes a while for players to adjust to a new coach, a new way of playing and a philosophy.

"Even if you have really good players, it doesn't just go like this. There are a lot of things we are doing behind the scenes for us to stay successful.

"I was lucky enough to come in when [Hayes] left the team in a really good place. But last season we had a year where a lot of important players left."

But captain Erin Cuthbert said she was "not really" surprised at how good their level has been so far.

"We had a good time to build in pre-season and a good trip away. The quality was always there, we just weren't clicking," she added.

"Manchester City ran away with the league in the end, but we were there or thereabouts. I feel this time the team's just gone up another level."

As well as adapting more to Bompastor's ways, and adding defensive solidity to a creative frontline, work has gone into improving the club's culture.

Cuthbert said before Wednesday's win there was "really good momentum and a good feeling" in the squad - so can they kick on now?

"For me, the mental aspects and cultural aspects are just as important," admitted Bompastor.

"We probably needed to rebuild a little bit of that going into this new season. We reflected a lot on how we wanted to set up the process for that.

"Right now, we are in a good place. When you are able to get good results, it's not only about the tactical aspects. It also has to be about mentality, culture and values.

"I think we have clarity on where we want to go as a team and how we want to get there, and that's just as important."

articles.title: Estevao: Why is the Brazilian becoming Chelsea's forgotten man?
articles.summary: Estevao faces limited opportunities at Chelsea as Pedro Neto’s form and competition for places in attack leave him struggling for game time under Xabi Alonso.
articles.body:
The last time Chelsea beat Liverpool , Estevao was the talk of the Premier League.

The Brazilian was still in his first couple of months at Stamford Bridge when his name hit the headlines after he scored the winner against the Premier League champions with practically the final kick of the match last October.

Fast forward 12 months, and Estevao is beginning to attract attention for all the wrong reasons as he struggles to force his way into Xabi Alonso's side.

The 19-year-old, who joined Chelsea from Palmeiras last summer, was conspicuous by his absence on Wednesday night as Chelsea were knocked out of the Carabao Cup following a penalty shootout loss to Liverpool at Anfield.

The Blues had taken the lead in the first half through Morgan Rogers, but they failed to kick on after Cody Gakpo quickly restored parity for the hosts.

Most concerning for Estevao, though, was that as both teams pushed for a winner in the second half, Alonso never appeared to consider the forward.

The clearest indication of just how low Estevao sits in Alonso's pecking order came midway through the second half, when Alonso made a triple substitution in an attempt to turn the game in his side's favour.

One of the three changes was Emanuel Emegha, who had yet to feature for the Blues since his summer move from Strasbourg.

Just moments after that triple change, which brought Chelsea 's total number of substitutions to five, Estevao could be seen ending his warm-up and retreating to the bench.

It was another night of no action for the Brazilian.

Liverpool overcome Chelsea in tense penalty shootout

'Stutter' penalty back in the spotlight after Barco miss costs Chelsea

Sadly for Estevao, Wednesday night's situation at Anfield was nothing new for him.

The Brazilian has failed to make the starting XI in any of the eight Premier League matches since Alonso took charge of the Blues in the summer.

His total minutes for the campaign so far stand at an underwhelming 172, with 125 of those coming in the victories over Luton Town and Leeds United in the earlier rounds of the EFL Cup.

Yet even in the thrilling 6-3 win against Daniel Farke's side, which remains one of only two games he has started this campaign, he was withdrawn at half-time with Chelsea trailing 1-0.

After the fourth-round defeat by Liverpool , Alonso defended his decision not to play Estevao, hinting that the forward is still coming to grips with the physical demands of English football.

"We started with Pedro [Neto], Morgan [Rogers] and Danny Welbeck, and the game had very intense moments," said Alonso.

"We knew it was going to be physical, and Malo [Gusto] had cramps, so we were a bit forced with substitutions. The season is going to be very long, and there will be moments for everyone."

When asked directly about the Brazilian, Alonso added: "He could be happier. He wants to play. I'm sure Estevao will have his moment, it is my responsibility.

"We know the game in England is really intense, and you need to be up for it. Estevao is in his second season. The season is going to be long."

Neto's revival and attacking firepower limit Estevao's chances

One of the main reasons behind Estevao's exile has been the form of Pedro Neto.

It was only a couple of months ago that Portugal international Neto looked destined to leave Chelsea , only two years after joining from Wolverhampton Wanderers.

The 26-year-old was linked with a move to Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli, but he ultimately remained at Stamford Bridge.

That decision appears to have been influenced by Alonso, who has underlined his faith in Neto by handing him seven starts in eight Premier League matches this season.

His success out on the right - which also happens to be Estevao's favoured position - has meant opportunities have been few and far between for the Brazilian.

He has primarily been deployed as a right-sided wing-back in Alonso's 3-4-2-1 system, with his Premier League experience and greater defensive solidity compared to Estevao seemingly winning over the Spaniard.

After an impressive start to the campaign, in which he has scored four goals in 11 matches, Neto was rewarded with a new six-year deal at Stamford Bridge.

"He's a player who is a little bit of a victim of the system," former Reading midfielder Jobi McAnuff told Sky Sports.

"Alonso tends to play Neto in that hybrid wing-back role, expecting him to get high up the pitch as well. Maybe he doesn't feel that suits Estevao, and I don't feel it does either."

One area that has not been a problem for the Blues this season is attack, with the forward positions firmly in the hands of Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Rogers, who has made a spectacular start to life at Stamford Bridge following his £117m move from Aston Villa .

Against Liverpool , though, Estevao couldn't even get a look-in despite Chelsea being without the suspended Palmer and the injured Joao Pedro.

"How Estevao has not got on the pitch tonight, I do not know," said former Crystal Palace forward Clinton Morrison.

"He must be thinking, 'What do I have to do? We have injuries to two of the star players up front, and I'm still not getting on the pitch'."

Estevao will be hoping he can follow in the footsteps of Neto and revive his Stamford Bridge career.

articles.title: Carabao Cup: 'Stutter' penalty back under debate after Barco miss costs Chelsea
articles.summary: The stuttering run-up for penalties has been called 'naive' as players continue to try to deceive goalkeepers with a stop-start approach - but why?
articles.body:
The pros and cons of a stuttering run-up are under debate after two crucial penalty misses in the Carabao Cup last 16.

Chelsea midfielder Valentin Barco missed the Blues' fourth penalty in their entertaining shootout defeat by Liverpool when he hit the post after a stuttered run-up.

Xabi Alonso's side would be in the EFL Cup quarter-finals had he scored, but they crashed out as defender Wesley Fofana sent one in sudden death high into the Kop at Anfield.

Barco's miss came after Arsenal midfielder Bruno Guimaraes had his spot-kick saved after a similar 'stutter' run-up as the Gunners crashed out against League Two Fleetwood Town on Tuesday night.

Both were shown how to do it by Liverpool defender Joe Gomez - a player who has never scored a senior goal in 319 professional appearances - who rifled the winning penalty into the top corner after a simple run-up.

Players opt for the stutter in a bid to trick the goalkeeper into giving them a clue as to which way they will dive.

The problem is it can backfire spectacularly if the goalkeeper holds their nerve or - in Barco's case - the taker fails to hit the target.

Former Chelsea defender Cesar Azpilicueta told ITV: "Every player picks his style where he feels confident, and for Valentin Barco, I believe that is his way of shooting it. I don't believe that was his first time, I hope not!"

The 'stutter' penalty became a theme of this year's World Cup . There were 26 at the summer's tournament but 11 were missed.

The stop-start run-up technique does not have a strict definition but a player is allowed, under Fifa rules, to stop or feint in the run-up as long as they don't do it directly before kicking the ball.

Even Harry Kane tried it in the summer and missed. His stuttering run-up led to Croatia goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic saving his penalty in England's 4-2 win.

But because Livakovic came off his line early, Kane got a retake and smashed it home with a straightforward approach.

Arsenal and Brazil midfielder Guimaraes was one of those 11 to miss at the World Cup but did not change his approach at Fleetwood.

Some players have used it to their advantage. Brazil icon Pele was famous for it while Cristiano Ronaldo has used it with both success and failure.

Manchester United 's Bruno Fernandes, former Chelsea and Arsenal midfielder Jorginho and Wolves striker Raul Jimenez are others who often use the 'stutter' style.

"I wouldn't allow it if I was a manager," former Liverpool midfielder Danny Murphy told TalkSport on Wednesday after Arsenal 's defeat the night before.

"It is ridiculous, self-indulgence, a player trying to be the centre of attention.

"When they do the stutter they think the keeper might go, but they aren't going that early, they aren't being tricked any more. It is naive."

But former Liverpool and Chelsea full-back Glen Johnson had a different view and pointed to the fact that Barco missed by mere inches.

"I like the technique," he told ITV. "It gives the players a bit of time.

"W what confused me about that one [from Barco] is usually players are watching the keeper. He has moved, he has got it right and gone the right way but lifted it in the air for no reason.

"You have the whole goal to shoot at and that is the surprising part. He has already beaten the goalkeeper, he doesn't have to hit it into the top corner.

"If he puts that ball three inches to the right you would say it is the best penalty you have seen."

It will not go down as a goal in the record books but Gomez got the feeling of seeing one of his shots hit the back of the net for the first time as a senior player.

It is remarkable that in 319 games for Charlton Athletic, Liverpool and England, the 29-year-old defender has never got on the scoresheet.

But Gomez looked like a veteran finisher when he powered his penalty - which was the penultimate of the shootout before Fofana missed - into the top corner in front of the Kop.

"Everyone is on edge and we want to win," Gomez told ITV.

"For me it is the moment I was thinking about and anticipating. It was nice it went in."

articles.title: Tetchy handshake typifies McInnes' 'topsy-turvy' Tynecastle return
articles.summary: Tetchy handshake typifies McInnes' 'topsy-turvy' Tynecastle return
articles.body:
Hearts head coach Wouter Vrancken spent his pre-match interview calling for focus and insisting he would "not be getting busy" with the tensions surrounding Rangers boss Derek McInnes' hostile return to Tynecastle.

By the end of the first half, the Belgian was in the referee's book before getting involved with a frosty handshake and exchange of words with his counterpart after a thrilling 2-2 draw .

Vrancken being swept up with the emotion told the story of a captivating encounter, which his depleted side looked set to win after fighting back from a goal down.

But a late Olwethu Makhanya header rescued a point for McInnes, who played the pantomime villain on a night that typified the Scottish Premiership's box-office drama.

Asked about the tetchy post-match handshake between the managers, the Rangers boss responded with tongue in cheek.

"I thought [Vrancken] was going to thank me for leaving him such a strong squad," McInnes told BBC Scotland. "He's been very lucky to inherit such a strong squad of players."

Makhanya rescues Rangers on hostile Hearts return for McInnes

McInnes admits 'guilt' over Hearts exit for Rangers

After admitting he felt "guilt" over his summer exit to Rangers after taking Hearts to within minutes of the title, McInnes accepted he was in for a tasty return.

"It was exactly what I thought it would be," he said of his reception. "It's football, it's Scottish football."

The 55-year-old still hopes "history can be kind" regarding his relationship with Hearts fans after a brief but memorable tenure in Gorgie.

His immediate concern, however, will be addressing the faults of a disjointed display as Saturday's League Cup semi-final with former club Aberdeen looms.

McInnes said his side were fortunate to go into the break ahead after Kevin Kelsy's opener came from slack Hearts play and lamented a lack of control in a "very topsy-turvy game".

"We scored a brilliant goal but didn't do that enough," the Rangers manager added.

"I don't think any team really grabbed the game and controlled the game, but I think Hearts had more opportunities to play in our half.

"When we did get a chance to transition on them, we never quite looked after the ball well enough.

"The top end of my side, they're very young and sometimes they need to come through these types of games and atmospheres, but we have to say we didn't play to our level."

Vrancken hails fighting spirit of depleted Hearts

For Vrancken, the Hearts boss was unsure what was behind the awkward post-match exchange. "You have to ask him," he said of McInnes.

The 47-year-old was also unclear of the severity of makeshift full-back Rogers Mato's first-half injury, which could potentially add to a long list of absentees with Sunday's League Cup semi-final against rivals Hibernian next up.

Although Vrancken was left disappointed by the decision to award Rangers the free-kick that led to their late leveller, he hailed the fight of his depleted team, who were relentless in their fightback and looked the fitter side despite a hectic schedule.

"We've lost two points. We deserved to win," he told BBC Scotland. "We played a really good first half, made a little mistake and it cost us. After that we made up for it with the performance.

"This team keeps believing, when you see the situation we are in. We have extra games, one day less recovery, all those things matter.

"When you see them battle and fight for each other, that's the pleasure I have as a coach."

articles.title: Pat McAfee Details Death Threats, Security Measures After Utah's Apology for Video
articles.summary: Pat McAfee's comments about Utah on College GameDay and the university's subsequent apology has generated plenty of attention, and the ESPN commentator posted a lengthy message on social media addressing a number of topics on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Pat McAfee's comments about Utah on College GameDay and the university's subsequent apology has generated plenty of attention, and the ESPN commentator posted a lengthy message on social media addressing a number of topics on Wednesday.

He shared screenshots of threatening messages he received on social media and added, "I've stayed away from my mentions and DM's this month since these back to back days but.. I'm sure if I went in there now, I'd find some wishes for and threats of death for me."

The former NFL player also opened up about a specific experience on College GameDay ahead of a Tennessee game and discussed the enhanced security measures that included presence from the FBI, Tennessee State Police, the Knoxville Police Department and university police.

"I'm trying my best in real time but.. I am to talk about sports and care about the future of sports," McAfee wrote. "I owe everything to sports. I'm grateful as hell to do what I do. I literally try to love every minute of the incredible opportunities I get to experience but.. it's certainly all a much different life than I could've ever expected.

"I try to give everything I have, all the time.. I am very sorry to those that despise me."

The message comes after the University of Utah released a statement Monday taking "full accountability" for a video posted on social media:

As The Athletic's Chris Vannini noted, McAfee addressed the situation during his show Monday and said he was "uncomfortable" during the College GameDay broadcast at Utah and regarding a social media video posted by some students doing an impression of him.

The university posted the video on its official Instagram page, although it later deleted it.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo beats Lionel Messi to win inaugural BOAT award for 2008 Manchester United season
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has been named the inaugural winner of the BOAT (Ballon d'Or of All Time) award, with fans voting his 2008 campaign at Manchester United
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo has been named the inaugural winner of the BOAT (Ballon d'Or of All Time) award, with fans voting his 2008 campaign at Manchester United as the greatest individual season in the history of football's most prestigious individual honour.Introduced by France Football, the award was designed to spark debate over which Ballon d'Or-winning campaign deserved to be considered the greatest of all time. Ronaldo came out on top after a fan-driven voting process, beating long-time rival Lionel Messi to the honour.Fans favoured Ronaldo's first Ballon d'Or-winning season in 2008 over Messi's remarkable 91-goal calendar year in 2012, a record that still stands.Unlike the traditional Ballon d'Or, where an international panel of prominent journalists determines the winner, the BOAT award allowed fans to cast their votes digitally. The voting list featured some of football's most celebrated names, including Johan Cruyff, Michel Platini, Marco van Basten, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, Kevin Keegan and Franz Beckenbauer. Real Madrid legend Alfredo Di Stefano and Brazilian great Ronaldo Nazario were also among the nominees.The voting process required participants to pay one euro, with organisers offering an additional incentive by entering voters into a prize draw for two tickets to the 2027 Ballon d'Or ceremony.The initiative attracted considerable interest, with thousands participating in the contest. More than 5,000 individuals voted multiple times in an effort to help their preferred player or campaign finish on top.Ronaldo and Messi dominated the final rankings, occupying the first 12 positions between them. The run was broken at 13th place by Brazil's Ronaldo Nazario, whose 2002 Ballon d'Or-winning campaign was the next highest-ranked season outside the pair.Ronaldo's victory adds another chapter to his long-running rivalry with Messi, with fans now having delivered their verdict on which of their standout Ballon d'Or-winning campaigns deserves the ultimate recognition.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El autor del meme que indigna a China rompe su silencio: "¿Me demandará Mbappé?"
articles.standfirst: Younes Khelifi (frenchaicovers) explica que "no me siento mal, pero resulta extraño pensar que, en cierto modo, soy el origen de todo esto".
articles.summary: Younes Khelifi (frenchaicovers) explica que "no me siento mal, pero resulta extraño pensar que, en cierto modo, soy el origen de todo esto".
articles.body: Younes Khelifi, un francés conocido como 'frenchaicovers' en X (Twitter), es el creador del polémico meme en el que Kylian Mbappé aparece con los rasgos de Mao Zedong y que tanto problemas le está generando al futbolista francés, al Real Madrid y a LaLiga. Al crear un montaje de vídeo de Mbappé con música comunista china en el verano de 2023, no sabía la tormenta que iba a desatar tres años después. 'Frenchaicovers' ha explicado en 'So Foot' que "fui uno de los primeros en hacer 'deepfakes' de este tipo; de hecho, ya había ganado algo de notoriedad por otros memes. Pero es verdad que, en esta ocasión, ha alcanzado una magnitud increíble". "No me siento mal, pero resulta extraño pensar que, en cierto modo, soy el origen de todo esto. Al principio, solo hice esto para reírme con mis amigos, y ahora veo cómo el asunto circula y crece ante mis propios ojos", reconoce el autor del meme de Mbappé en modo Mao Zedong que tanto ha indignado a China. Sobre el impacto que ha tenido este meme desvela que "estaba en la cama y no paraba de decirme: '¡Pero qué locura es esta!'. Así que, cinco minutos después, tuiteo: 'Me levanto y veo que he provocado un incidente diplomático'. (Risas). Sinceramente, al ver eso, me pregunté si podría tener consecuencias legales. ¿Me iba a demandar el clan Mbappé y exigirme una indemnización? Pero me informé y no me preocupa demasiado. Lo primero que pensé fue, literalmente, lo que puse en el tuit: 'Si me llevas a los tribunales, Mbappé, ¡yo quedo financieramente arruinado!'. (Risas). En fin, ¡comparado con él, estoy más que hundido! A lo largo del día vi cómo se desarrollaba todo, hasta que esta mañana me encuentro con que el asunto acaba en la portada de L’Équipe. Fui a comprar cuatro ejemplares". "Me he planteado seriamente si debería contactar con la embajada de Francia en China para asegurarme de que todo está bien, teniendo en cuenta el meme y lo que acaba de ocurrir. Soy consciente de que es una petición un tanto peculiar, incluso ridícula, pero prefiero estar seguro", apuntó. 'Frenchaicovers' reconoce que "no imaginé que esto fuera a traspasar las fronteras de Francia" y que "sinceramente, me da un poco de pena por Mbappé. Nadie tenía mala intención y, al final, ha tenido consecuencias".

articles.title: Radiografía de los 100 goles de Mbappé con el Real Madrid: el ariete que se fabrica sus propios goles
articles.standfirst: Su doblete en el Camp Nou le sitúa entre los cinco blancos que menos partidos necesitaron para llegar a la centena
articles.summary: Su doblete en el Camp Nou le sitúa entre los cinco blancos que menos partidos necesitaron para llegar a la centena
articles.body: Kylian Mbappé marcó los dos goles del Real Madrid en el Spotify Camp Nou y el segundo llevaba una cifra pegada. Era el número cien con la camiseta blanca, un listón que solo veintitrés futbolistas habían alcanzado antes que él en la historia del club. El escenario encajaba con su trayectoria, porque el Barcelona es el rival al que más ha marcado desde que llegó a Madrid, con ocho goles en siete partidos. Según Opta, ningún jugador ha anotado más que él en sus siete primeros Clásicos en lo que va de siglo. Llegar a cien suele ser cuestión de años. Mbappé lo ha hecho en 116 partidos y solo cuatro jugadores en toda la historia del Madrid necesitaron menos: Puskas (101), Cristiano Ronaldo(105) y Pahiño y Alfredo Di Stéfano (114). Su media de 0,86 goles por partido es la cuarta mejor entre los blancos que han alcanzado la centena, por detrás de Cristiano (1,03), Puskas (0,92) y Pahiño (0,87). Las cifras de todos ellos corresponden a su etapa completa en el club, de modo que la de Mbappé es la única que sigue moviéndose. Entre los delanteros de su generación, solo Harry Kane ha marcado más goles desde la 2024-25 en las cinco grandes ligas: 112 en 114 partidos, frente a los 100 en 116 de Mbappé. Haaland, tercero, se queda en 85. La comparación entre los dos primeros muestra dos maneras de llegar a esas cifras. Kane convierte el 26,11% de sus remates y supera en 24,71 goles lo que esperaban los modelos de sus ocasiones. Mbappé convierte el 19,38% y supera su xG en 10,24, pero lo hace sobre un volumen que nadie más ha igualado desde que llegó al Madrid, con 89,76 de xG, el mejor registro de las cinco grandes ligas, y 516 remates, algo más de cuatro por partido. Ese caudal le permite marcar un gol cada 95 minutos, por delante de Haaland (107) y solo por detrás de Kane (80). Una de las señas de Mbappé es la facilidad para generarse el gol sin esperar un pase. Ha marcado 17 desde fuera del área, el registro más alto de las cinco grandes ligas desde su llegada a la casa blanca, y 19 de sus goles llegaron tras una conducción de cinco metros o más con el balón controlado, una cifra que solo superan Raphinha (23) y Olise (21). Su mapa de toques, con 5.408 acciones, lo coloca sobre todo en el carril izquierdo, por delante del área, y los 84 goles con la derecha encajan en muchos casos con ese recorrido en diagonal hacia el centro. Solo dos han sido de cabeza y 14 los ha firmado con la izquierda. A ese reparto se suman los penaltis. 21 de los 100 goles llegaron desde los once metros, sobre 26 lanzamientos, y 17 desde fuera del área, de modo que los 62 restantes son de jugada dentro del área. La curva de Mbappé en el Madrid solo ha subido. En la 2024-25 marcó cada 107 minutos, en la 2025-26 cada 87' y en lo que va de curso cada 83', con 14 goles en 13 partidos, todos como titular. Si nos quedamos con el acierto, ha pasado del 18,14% al 21,88%, y el xG por partido ha crecido de 0,70 a 1,04. Los 14 goles de este año coinciden casi exactamente con un xG de 13,58, de modo que el aumento de producción nace de las ocasiones que recibe. Por entrenadores, su mejor tramo coincide con Xabi Alonso, con quien firmó 30 goles en 28 partidos, uno cada 75 minutos y un acierto del 22,56%. El más discreto llegó con Arbeloa, con 13 en 19 y un gol cada 115 minutos, aunque su xG en esos partidos (12,82) fue casi idéntico a sus goles. Con Ancelotti firmó 43 en 56 y con Mourinho suma 14 en 13. Por competiciones, lleva 67 goles en 75 partidos de LaLiga y 25 en 28 de Champions, el mismo 0,89 por encuentro en ambas. Marcó en su único partido de la Supercopa de Europa y en el de la Intercontinental, mientras que en la Supercopa de España y en el Mundial de Clubes se quedó en un gol por torneo, en tres partidos cada uno. El Barcelona encabeza la lista de víctimas, seguido de la Real Sociedad (siete goles en cinco partidos), el Villarreal y el Sevilla (cinco en cinco). Algunas noches pesan más que otras, como los cuatro goles al Olympiacos y los tres al Kairat, ambos en un único partido, o los cuatro al Manchester City en tres enfrentamientos. Entre sus socios, Vinicius es quien más veces le ha dado el pase del gol (13), seguido de Arda Güler (12) y Jude Bellingham (9). Entre los tres suman 34 de sus cien goles. Los cien ya están contados. Queda por ver cuánto resiste el 0,86 cuando los partidos se cuenten por cientos. Cristiano terminó en 1,03 tras 438 y Benzema en 0,55 tras 648.

articles.title: White scores 100th MLS goal as Whitecaps beat San Diego 4-1 to strengthen hold on 1st place
articles.summary: VANCOUVER, British Columbia (AP) — Brian White scored his 100th MLS goal, Ryan Gauld had a goal and an assist, and the Vancouver Whitecaps beat San Diego 4-1...
articles.body:
VANCOUVER, British Columbia (AP) — Brian White scored his 100th MLS goal, Ryan Gauld had a goal and an assist, and the Vancouver Whitecaps beat San Diego 4-1 on Wednesday night.

Vancouver (17-8-7) extended its lead in the Western Conference to four points over second-place Dallas, which lost to Columbus earlier.

San Diego (8-13-11), which was eliminated from playoff contention, had its winless streak stretched to 10 games (0-5-5).

Aleksa Cvetković, in just his fourth start since joining the Whitecaps in August, scored his first MLS goal in the 24th minute on a redirection of Mathias Laborda's pass across the goal. White headed in a curling pass by Oliver Larraz in the 41st for his 18th MLS goal this season.

The 30-year-old White has 98 goals across all competitions since joining the Whitecaps in 2021. White became the 17th player in MLS history to score 100 goals.

Gauld scored on a diving header in the 66th for Vancouver's 67th goal — the most the Caps have scored during a MLS regular season. Bruno Caicedo beat goalkeeper Pablo Sisniega in the 76th on a two-on-one breakaway for a 4-0 lead.

Onni Valakari put San Diego on the board in the 83rd with a header.

articles.title: El Real Madrid pone la directa
articles.standfirst: Suma cinco victorias seguidas, una cifra en la élite que sólo supera el PSG
articles.summary: Suma cinco victorias seguidas, una cifra en la élite que sólo supera el PSG
articles.body: El Real Madrid se fue al parón de selecciones con las heridas de la derrota en el derbi. El resultado, el juego, la polémica, la brecha de seis puntos con el Barcelona... El riesgo de caer en el abismo de una temporada dramática.. Menos de dos meses después, a una semana vista del siguiente parón internacional, el equipo de Mourinho va lanzado. Desde el regreso del largo tramo de partidos de selecciones entre finales de septiembre y principios de octubre, el Madrid no ha hecho más que ganar. Son cinco triunfos consecutivos: tres de Liga (Villarreal, Sevilla y Barcelona) y dos en la Champions (Roma y Leipzig). El Madrid mira a su alrededor en la élite del fútbol europeo y solo ve a un equipo que mejora su rendimiento en las últimas semanas. Las cinco victorias consecutivas del conjunto blanco solo las supera un rival: el PSG. Después de un arranque de temporada errático, con una sola victoria en sus cinco primeros partidos, la de la Supercopa de Europa, el bicampeón de Europa acumula ya ocho triunfos seguidos. El resto de grandes de Europa se ha dejado victorias por el camino en el tramo que va desde el final del parón a hoy. El Barcelona, que contaba cada uno de sus partido por victorias, ha caído en los dos últimos. Sus rivales han sido, precisamente, PSG y Real Madrid. El Manchester City caminaba lanzado desde su derrota ante el Arsenal en la Community Shield (3-0), pero de sus últimos cuatro partidos ha caído en dos: PSG y Aston Villa. En España, el Atlético de Madrid es el equipo con mejor racha en la Liga: seis victorias consecutivas. Pero su cadena de triunfos se detuvo con el empate a uno ante el Stuttgart en la Liga de Campeones. Esas tablas impiden que su serie de victorias sea idéntica a la del PSG. Al margen de ese pleno de triuinfos de cinco partidos, el Madrid ha disparado sus buenas sensaciones como equipo. La victoria en el Camp Nou fue un golpe de autoridad. La sensación de que el equipo de Mourinho iba a aparecer en el feudo barcelonista para ser devorado menguó según se acercaba el partido. Y el duelo entre colosos dejó claro que el Madrid tiene armas de sobra para mirar a la cara a un Barcelona que parecía ir sin cadena. Antes de que las selecciones vuelvan a reclutar a sus jugadores, el Madrid tiene tres partidos. Tres citas fuera de casa en las que puede elevar su cuenta de victorias consecutivas hasta nueve. Para ello necesita imponerse este domingo en Santander, el miércoles en Atenas y el día 8 en Mestalla. Si lo consigue, llevará su contador a una cifra de triunfos consecutivos que no se ve desde el arranque de la temporada 2022-23. Entonces, el Madrid lo ganó todo desde la Supercopa de Europa, 2-0 al Eintracht en Varsovia, hasta el empate sorprendente ante Osasuna en Chamartín: 1-1, con un penalti fallado por Benzema. Ajeno a las olas de euforia y de hundimientos, Mourinho ya lanzó un avios a navegantes: "De nada vale esto si no ganamos en Santander".

articles.title: Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga face long road to redemption in China
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga have apologised for the superstar striker's comments about Mao Zedong, but the damage to their reputation in China won...
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga have apologised for the superstar striker's comments about Mao Zedong, but the damage to their reputation in China won't be easily or quickly repaired, experts say.

The France captain, one of the best footballers on the planet, is at the centre of a major row after a video emerged this week of him appearing to make fun of former leader Mao.

Mbappe talked about being amused by an internet meme of his face photoshopped onto "some guy, think he's a Chinese dictator".

Mao remains officially revered as the hero of the communist revolution and founder of the People's Republic of China.

He is blamed by historians for millions of deaths, but publicly mocking him is taboo, and Mbappe's remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure or entity to infuriate Beijing.

Major Chinese brands cut ties with the 27-year-old, and Spanish top-flight matches will be pulled from state television broadcaster CCTV.

Chinese state media and social media users lined up to lambast Mbappe, although they were left in the dark about what exactly he said.

China has the world's second-biggest economy and can be hugely lucrative, and within two days the striker, his club Real Madrid, and La Liga all apologised.

A spokesman for China's foreign ministry said the Beijing government took Mbappe's apology "seriously".

"Viewed from a calm, objective and emotion-free standpoint, this is clearly a very damaging incident," Yan Qiang, a veteran sports commentator, told AFP.

"It causes serious damage to the image of La Liga and Real Madrid in China.

"In the age of the mobile internet things blow up on social media quickly and emotions run high.

"An apology does not necessarily mean the end of the story.

"It's better to have an apology than no apology at all, but it's definitely not the end of the story."

The Mbappe furore and fallout is not an unfamiliar tale.

Various overseas sports leagues or players have found themselves in hot water for comments on topics that are politically sensitive to China.

China effectively cut ties with the NBA in 2019 after then-Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey tweeted his support for Hong Kong protesters.

NBA executives said Morey had the right to freedom of expression. In contrast, La Liga immediately distanced itself from what Mbappe said.

The NBA, which along with football is the most popular sport in China, was wiped from CCTV for more than a year.

NBA pre-season matches only returned to China last year.

Australian National University lecturer Debby Chan called the NBA case -- and now Mbappe -- an illustration of China's consumer nationalism, where online sentiment and state media converge into "a spiral of outrage".

NBA commissioner Adam Silver said the league lost "hundreds of millions of dollars" over the split.

Spanish football also has a lot to lose.

A source within La Liga told AFP that China and the United States alone finance the "majority" of international broadcasting rights, which were valued at 748 million euros ($834 million) for the 2024-25 season.

According to the Real Madrid-affiliated newspaper Marca, the Madrid club generates between 10 and 15 percent of its sales of jerseys and merchandise in China.

Real Madrid also counts Chinese companies among its main sponsors, with Hisense, sports betting firm Kaiyun Sports, and Linglong Tire all featuring prominently.

Adam Zhang, founder of the Beijing-based Key-Solution Sports Consulting, said showing fast and heartfelt remorse was the first step.

"This will influence the decision on whether to continue the broadcast ban and, if so, for how long," he told AFP.

Sports commentator Yan cast doubt on whether the reputation of Mbappe, whose face has adorned drinks bottles and advertising campaigns in China, can ever fully recover.

"Judging by commercial sponsorships and big ad campaigns he appeared in during the World Cup, he has a huge influence in China," he said.

"If that influence can't be sustained there can be no talk of commercial interests, and La Liga and Real Madrid will definitely be badly affected."

Yan said it was "genuinely hard to predict" what happens next.

"In the short term, I'm certainly not optimistic," he added.

"If they want to repair their image and the relationship, their future actions and behaviour will be key."
authors: Peter Stebbings with Luna Lin in Beijing

articles.title: Vancouver Whitecaps take control of West on record-breaking night
articles.summary: By Alex CalabreseVancouver Whitecaps FC are storming to the finish line of the 2026 MLS regular season.With a resounding 4-1 win over San Diego FC at BC Plac...
articles.body:
Vancouver Whitecaps FC are storming to the finish line of the 2026 MLS regular season.

With a resounding 4-1 win over San Diego FC at BC Place and other results going their way on Wednesday night, the 'Caps solidified their lead atop the Western Conference table (58 points).

With that, Jesper Sørensen's side are closing in on securing the No. 1 seed in the West and, thus, home-field advantage all the way through the 2026 Audi MLS Cup Playoffs and possibly the Dec. 18 final.

"I just have a good feeling about how we played. I know that everybody's focusing on the standings and stuff," Sørensen told reporters postmatch. "Last year we lost our last game and came in second instead of first, and it looked to be going up against.

"So it's more, it's more important how we play and play."

A year on from reaching the MLS Cup and Concacaf Champions Cup finals, the Whitecaps are looking to take a step further in 2026.

With their four goals on Wednesday, they have smashed their club record for goals in a season , reaching 67 with two games to spare.

Summer U22 Initiative signing Aleksa Cvetković got things started early, finishing off a penalty box sequence with for first MLS goal. Talisman Brian White headed home just before halftime to double the lead, and Ryan Gauld extended the scoreline to 3-0 early in the second half.

Superstar Designated Player Thomas Müller was also introduced in the second half, marking his return from injury after almost a month out and adding an exciting boost to Vancouver's attack.

Young Ecuadorian star Bruno Caicedo added the exclamation point with the record-breaking goal in the 76th minute, finishing off a fast break with his sixth tally of the season. The 21-year-old winger was named 15th on the league's 22 Under 22 last week, and is quickly emerging as one of the MLS' most exciting young prospects.

White's first-half goal was his 18th of the campaign, but more importantly, it was his 100th career MLS goal. The former Red Bull New York SuperDraft pick has come into his own since moving to Vancouver in 2021, and now deservingly sits among the league's top strikers amid a career-best 18g/2a in 2026.

"Something I've always wanted to get to and had my eyes on, if I'm being honest, to get to 100 goals," said White. "But at the end of the day, you want to win championships with the team to see like those things are nice, like you said, but you want to win MLS Cup.

"I would win MLS Cup, and that's first and foremost on my mind."

Vancouver need just one more win to secure the top seed in the West, with which they ensure home-field advantage in the playoffs at least up until the conference finals.

It would also secure qualification to the 2027 Champions Cup.

They'll have two chances to do so, traveling to Seattle Sounders FC on Sunday (3:30 pm ET | Apple TV ) before hosting CF Montréal on Decision Day.

"We are ready to attack the last two games," said Sørensen. "And hopefully that will be enough also to win the Western Conference regular season."

articles.title: Papin apunta al gran pecado de Mbappé que le condenó para ganar el Balón de Oro: "Refleja cómo es él"
articles.standfirst: "La estrategia de comunicación de Mbappé le ha perjudicado mucho.Es una lástima, teniendo en cuenta sus cualidades y el club en el que juega (el Real Madrid)"
articles.summary: "La estrategia de comunicación de Mbappé le ha perjudicado mucho.Es una lástima, teniendo en cuenta sus cualidades y el club en el que juega (el Real Madrid)"
articles.body: Jean-Pierre Papin, mítico delantero francés ganador del Balón de Oro en 1991, cree que la estrategia comunicativa de Kylian Mbappé de cara al Balón de Oro terminó volviéndose en su contra. El exfutbolista de 62 años considera que declaraciones como "no hubo nadie mejor que yo esta temporada" penalizaron al futbolista del Real Madrid, que quedó segundo en las votaciones por detrás de Harry Kane. Mbappé ya terminó séptimo en 2017, cuarto en 2018, sexto en 2019, noveno en 2021, sexto en 2022, tercero en 2023, sexto en 2024 y séptimo en 2025. Jean-Pierre Papin defendió en el programa 'Rothen s’enflamme' de RMC Sport que las numerosas intervenciones de Mbappé en los medios, destinadas a defender su trayectoria, terminaron volviéndose en su contra. "La estrategia de comunicación de Mbappé le ha perjudicado mucho. Refleja, en cierto modo, cómo es él. Es una lástima, teniendo en cuenta sus cualidades y el club en el que juega (el Real Madrid)", compartió el ex de Olympique, Milan y Bayern. Papin subrayó que "Mbappé me recuerda un poco a Cristiano Ronaldo: los demás tenían que ponerse a su servicio". "En cuanto a eficacia, no está lejos de lo que lograba Cristiano Ronaldo. Pero su estrategia de comunicación le ha jugado una mala pasada. Estoy convencido de que ganará el Balón de Oro; tiene las cualidades necesarias para conseguirlo. No era una cuestión de "ahora o nunca". Fue una buena oportunidad, sí, pero todavía le queda camino por recorrer", apuntó el goleador de Boulogne-sur-Mer.
